subject: EdgeCloud / Acme on‑prem VPC: deployment synthesis & runbook gaps
messages:
From: Rowan Li <rowan.li@edgecloud.com>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-25T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Onboarding: EdgeCloud / Acme - On-prem VPC deployment draft

Hi Avery and team,

Thanks for the intro — attaching our initial schematic for the on-prem VPC attachment (edgecloud-schematic-v1.png). High level: Acme wants the control plane to remain logically managed by Redwood but terminate inside their VPC with mutual TLS, while the inference data plane stays fully on-prem for residency.

We have a couple of open questions before the architecture review call:
- Can Redwood confirm the expected outbound ports and hostnames for control plane connectivity (we only have a vague 443 requirement today)?
- Any constraints around using a shared NAT vs HA NAT pairs?
- Proposed fallback behaviour if the control plane becomes unreachable during model traffic spikes.

I can loop in Acme Ops if you want concrete subnet ranges ahead of the call. We're aiming to run a small canary next week if the runbook alignment is quick.

Rowan
Rowan Li
Solutions Engineer, EdgeCloud Solutions
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Rowan Li <rowan.li@edgecloud.com>, ops@acme.example
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-25T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: EdgeCloud / Acme - On-prem VPC deployment draft

Rowan — thanks for the schematic. Uploading a short Redwood runbook excerpt for our expected attachment flow (redwood-onprem-runbook-v1.3.pdf). High-level points and asks:

1) Control plane connectivity
- We require mTLS to api-control.redwood.example:443 from nodes in the customer VPC. Client certs will be provisioned during onboarding via the control handshake.
- Healthchecks: outbound HTTPS TCP/443 with SNI to api-control.redwood.example and telemetry endpoints.

2) Data plane and KV cache
- Data plane stays on-prem; Redis/KV cache sync uses gRPC over TLS on port 9411 (cluster-internal). Peering or routing must allow node-to-node connectivity for cache replication across racks.

3) Fallback and canary
- If control plane is unreachable for X minutes, nodes should switch to local degraded model family (redwood-lite or pinned quantized variant) and serve from local cache.
- We prefer a 5% canary for the initial test with a fast rollback window.

Operational asks before the canary:
- Provide explicit subnet ranges and NAT/egress model (HA NAT vs single NAT)
- Confirm firewall rules or a list of blocked ports on Acme edge appliances
- Approve a one-hour window for canary connectivity tests on 2028-07-28 (proposed).

Can you provide a quick note with subnets and NAT topology? I'll also keep Marissa and Jonas on the thread to capture any runbook delta items.

Thanks,
Avery Johnson
Product Manager, Deployments
Redwood Inference

Quick notes from an ops/readiness perspective (copying Rowan so Acme sees the constraints up front):
- Watch for asymmetric routing if Acme insists on hairpinning through an external NAT. We need bi-directional flows for healthchecks and telemetry.
- Recommend HA NAT pairs (active/standby) and at least two egress IPs to avoid connection tracking saturation during token-refresh churn.
- Ports we expect open: 443 (control, telemetry), 9411 (cache gRPC), 15000-15010 (agent diagnostics/trace ingestion). If Acme has strict outbound allowlists we'll need an ACL snapshot.

Attaching a short summary of items I want captured in the runbook (attachment-summary.txt). Will flag anything requiring SOC2 evidence separately.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Technical Program Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-07-26T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: EdgeCloud / Acme - On-prem VPC deployment draft

Thanks — latching onto Marissa's ops points and putting concrete networking guidance below. Quoting Avery's ask for clarity:

> We require mTLS to api-control.redwood.example:443 from nodes in the customer VPC. Client certs will be provisioned during onboarding via the control handshake.

Concrete network requirements (for the runbook):
- Outbound hosts: api-control.redwood.example (443), telemetry.redwood.example (443), s3-backup.redwood.example (443) for snapshots. All over TLS with SNI.
- Outbound ports: 443 for control/telemetry, 9411 for cache sync (gRPC/TLS), 22 only for scheduled debug windows (by exception).
- DNS resolution must be permitted from nodes; we validate TLS certs and SNI on connect.
- KV cache replication: gRPC over TLS on 9411; nodes perform peer discovery over control channel but will open direct TCP sessions for replication. Ensure intra-VPC routing allows node-to-node flows on that port.
- Fallback policy: if control plane handshake fails for 3 consecutive minutes, node flips to degraded model family and serves from local cache. If control plane returns, node performs a fast-sync of KV and switches back during a low QPS window.

Operational tests we need from Acme before the canary:
1) Confirm NAT topology and provide two egress IPs for allowlist.
2) Run a connectivity check from an agent host to api-control.redwood.example:443 and report TLS handshake SNI result.
3) Allow our canary IPs (listed in runbook delta) for a scheduled 09:00 PT window on 2028-07-28.

Deliverables attached: vpc-attachment-diagram-v2.drawio and a patch to the runbook with the above ports/hosts (runbook-delta-avery-20280725.patch).

Jonas Weber
Staff Engineer, Inference Networking
Redwood Inference

Avery / Jonas — sending the subnet list and NAT topology as requested (acme-subnets.csv). Acme confirms:
- Subnets: 10.10.0.0/22 (control agents), 10.10.4.0/22 (inference nodes), 10.10.8.0/24 (management)
- NAT: HA NAT pair in front of egress with two public IPs; will permit outbound to the hosts and ports you listed.
- Can confirm DNS and TLS handshake are not blocked.

We agree to the 09:00 PT canary on 2028-07-28, limit to 5% traffic, and will standby the rollback contact (ops@acme.example). Please send the final runbook patch and the canary IPs so we can pre-seed allowlists.

Thanks,
Rowan
